He was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and the top prospect in his state, earning [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] honors in [[2018 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2018]]. Bazley initially committed to and signed with [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse]] but later chose to bypass college with intentions of joining the [[NBA G League]], a decision that drew national attention. However, he instead chose to train on his own for the entire season for the [[2019 NBA draft]]. Standing {{convert|6|ft|9|in|m|2}} and weighing {{convert|200|lbs|kg|0}}, he plays the [[small forward]] and [[power forward (basketball)|power forward]] positions. ==High school career== Bazley began playing high school basketball at [[Finneytown High School]] in [[Springfield Township, Hamilton County, Ohio|Springfield Township, Ohio]]. He was ruled ineligible for the first half of his freshman season.{{cite web |last1=Baum |first1=Adam |last2=Robbe |first2=Nick |title=Roger Bacon basketball looking to reload |url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/high-school/ohio-high-school/2014/11/28/roger-bacon-basketball-looking-reload/19631365/ |website=[[The Cincinnati Enquirer]] |accessdate=August 12, 2018 |date=November 28, 2014}} As a sophomore, Bazley started drawing interest from several college programs, including [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]] and [[West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball|West Virginia]].{{cite web |last1=Schmetzer |first1=Mark |title=Finneytown’s Bazley handles spotlight, roundball |url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/high-school/ohio-high-school/2015/12/22/finneytowns-bazley-handles-spotlight/77772006/ |website=[[The Cincinnati Enquirer]] |accessdate=August 12, 2018 |date=December 22, 2015}} On December 19, 2015, he posted 25 points, 15 rebounds, and 5 blocks against [[Woodward High School (Cincinnati, Ohio)|Woodward High School]]. After averaging 15.8 points, 12.4 rebounds, 3.8 assists, 2.4 blocks and 1.5 steals, he was named to the Division III Southwest Ohio all-district second team.{{cite web |title=SW Ohio All-District boys hoops teams named |url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/high-school/ohio-high-school/2016/03/03/sw-ohio-all-district-boys-hoops-teams-named/81261620/ |website=[[The Cincinnati Enquirer]] |accessdate=August 12, 2018 |date=March 3, 2016}}{{cite web |last1=Dyer |first1=Mike |title=Finneytown's Darius Bazley is ranked Ohio's No. 1 player in the 2018 class |url=https://www.wcpo.com/news/insider/finneytowns-darius-bazley-is-ranked-the-states-no-1-player-in-the-2018-class |publisher=[[WCPO-TV]] |accessdate=August 12, 2018 |date=June 20, 2016}} Entering his junior campaign, Bazley was the top-ranked player in Ohio. In July 2016, it was announced that he would transfer to [[Princeton High School (Ohio)|Princeton High School]] in [[Sharonville, Ohio]].{{cite web |last1=Dyer |first1=Mike |title=Finneytown basketball standout Darius Bazley transfers to Princeton |url=https://www.wcpo.com/sports/high-school-sports/ohio-high-school-sports/finneytown-basketball-standout-darius-bazley-transfers-to-princeton |publisher=[[WCPO-TV]] |accessdate=August 13, 2018 |date=July 30, 2016}} He was sidelined for his first 11 games because of transfer rules.{{cite web |title=Five things to know: Darius Bazley |url=https://www.usab.com/news-events/news/2018/03/hsum-features-bazley.aspx |publisher=[[USA Basketball]] |accessdate=August 13, 2018}} In August, Bazley committed to Ohio State, being rated a four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] by [[247Sports.com|247Sports]] at the time.{{cite web |last1=Landis |first1=Bill |title=Darius Bazley, Justin Ahrens -- pair of 2018 Ohio prospects -- commit to Ohio State basketball |url=https://www.cleveland.com/osu/index.ssf/2016/08/darius_bazley_justin_ahrens_--.html |website=[[The Plain Dealer]] |accessdate=August 13, 2018 |date=August 27, 2016}} On January 11, 2017, he debuted for Princeton, recording 11 points, 10 rebounds, 5 assists, and 3 steals in a loss at the Flyin' To The Hoop Invitational.{{cite web |last1=Dyer |first1=Mike |title=Princeton basketball standout Darius Bazley reflects on season debut |url=https://www.wcpo.com/news/insider/princeton-basketball-standout-darius-bazley-reflects-on-season-debut bball = yes }} ==Professional career== On March 30, 2018, Bazley announced that he would skip college with plans to join the [[NBA G League]] directly from high school.{{cite web |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |title=Five-star recruit Darius Bazley to decommit from Syracuse, join G League |url=http://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/22958288/five-star-recruit-darius-bazley-decommit-syracuse-join-g-league |website=[[ESPN]] |accessdate=August 13, 2018 |date=March 30, 2018}} In April, he hired sports agent [[Rich Paul]] of Klutch Sports Group.{{cite web |last1=Zagoria |first1=Adam |title=Darius Bazley Charts Yet Another Path to the N.B.A.: The Development League |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2018/04/23/sports/darius-bazley.html |website=[[The New York Times]] |accessdate=August 13, 2018 |date=April 23, 2018}} Syracuse head coach [[Jim Boeheim]], who Bazley was expected to play under in college before the move, responded, "I hope he does great. But I don't think it's the way it will be. I think it will be proven it's not the way to get to the NBA."{{cite web |last1=Clark |first1=Dave |title=Boeheim on Bazley: 'It's not the way to get to the NBA' |url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/high-school/ohio-high-school/2018/04/04/boeheim-bazley-its-not-way-get-nba/485595002/ |website=[[The Cincinnati Enquirer]] |accessdate=August 13, 2018 |date=April 4, 2018}} An article from [[Bleacher Report]] speculated that Bazley could be "the face of the end of [[Eligibility for the NBA draft|one-and-done]]" for [[NBA draft]] eligibility because of his decision.{{cite web |last1=Gardner |first1=David |title=Is Darius Bazley the face of the end of one-and-done? |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2787081-darius-bazley-nba-g-league-power-50 |publisher=[[Bleacher Report]] |accessdate=August 13, 2018 |date=July 23, 2018}} On August 27, Bazley announced that he would drop his G League plans altogether, opting instead to train on his own for the season.https://theathletic.com/489209/2018/08/27/darius-bazley-scraps-g-league-move-to-train-on-his-own-ahead-of-nba-draft/ On October 25, Bazley began a three-month internship with [[New Balance]] worth $1 million.https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/25074140/rich-paul-darius-bazley-1-million-internship-result-broken-system After concluding his internship, Bazley became one of the first players to enter the [[2019 NBA draft]],[https://lebronwire.usatoday.com/2019/04/01/did-darius-bazley-and-klutch-sports-make-the-right-call/ Did Darius Bazley and Klutch Sports make the right call?][https://pr.nba.com/early-entry-candidates-2019-draft/ NBA announces early entry candidates for 2019 NBA Draft presented by State Farm] later being named one of 77 overall prospects invited to the 2019 [[NBA Draft Combine]].[https://www.nba.com/article/2019/05/08/66-players-attend-nba-draft-combine Sixty-six players expected to attend NBA Draft Combine] ==References== {{Reflist|30em}} ==External links== *[https://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/b/bazley-darius.aspx USA Basketball bio] {{DEFAULTSORT:Bazley, Darius}} [[Category:2000 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players from Ohio]] [[Category:McDonald's High School All-Americans]] [[Category:Power forwards (basketball)]] [[Category:Small forwards]] [[Category:Sportspeople from Boston]] [[Category:Sportspeople from Cincinnati]]
